name: Tumari Kanuri
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only dialectology (Jarrett 1988), dialect survey (Bulakarima 1997) and a conjugation manual (Jarrett & Garba 2004); no phonology/grammar of Tumari

sources.citation: Awagana, Ari & Camille Lefebvre. 2025. L'œuvre en kanouri d'al-Hajj Musa ibn Hissein, un savant du Borno (Niger-Nigeria). Leiden: Brill (open access).
sources.note: Fig. 2 (p. 22) classifies Tumari under Kanouri 'Est' with Mowar; the translated Prietze remark on 'accent tonique' (orig. p. 135-136) concerns Manga/Borno Kanuri generally ('Les syllabes d'un mot semblent souvent être en équilibre..'), not Tumari.

sources.citation: Jarrett, Kevin. 2007. A dictionary of Manga, a Kanuri language of Eastern Niger and NE Nigeria. Edited by Roger Blench. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 162 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; Manga not Tumari. Tone-marked lexicon with a one-page editor's introduction (symbol conversions, 'Tone-marks sometimes omitted'); no prosody description.

sources.citation: Bulakarima, Shettima Umara. 1996. Kanembu-Kanuri relationship: a proposal. Berichte des Sonderforschungsbereichs 268, Bd. 8: 37-49.
sources.note: Nothing; tone-marked comparative wordlist only (per held text and sibling), no prose on prosody.

sources.citation: Jarrett, Kevin A. 1988. Dialectes et alphabétisation dans les écoles: une étude explorative de l'intercompréhension des différents dialectes kanuri du Niger. Journal of West African Languages 18(2): 105-124.
sources.note: Nothing. Tumari (Nguigmi) is one of the five test dialects; the only prosodic remark (sec. 2b) is generic: many African languages are tonal and tone/intonation are not represented in writing. No statement of tone or stress placement for any dialect.

sources.citation: Cyffer, Norbert. 1998. A Sketch of Kanuri. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. 80 pp. (and Hutchison, John P. 1981. The Kanuri Language: A Reference Grammar. Madison.)

sources.note: Authoritative statements that Kanuri is a tone language (Yerwa); would supply the family-level prosodic characterisation if a Tumari-specific source never surfaces (second-hand for Tumari).
